question: Your CI pipeline runs Claude Code to update GraphQL schema files in pull requests. The schema conventions live in .claude/rules/graphql.md with the frontmatter paths: ["schema/*.graphql"]. The schema files are spread across many directories, for example services/orders/api/order.graphql and libs/shared/types.graphql. CI logs show that Claude Code never applies the conventions when it edits these files. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The glob pattern matches only GraphQL files directly inside a root-level schema directory, so schema files in other directories never activate the rule.
options.reason: Glob patterns decide which files activate a path-specific rule; a type-based pattern such as **/*.graphql would match these files regardless of directory location.

options.text: A rule in .claude/rules/ applies only to files in the directory that contains the rule file, so it cannot reach files under services/ or libs/.
options.reason: Rule activation depends on the glob patterns in the YAML frontmatter paths field, not on where the rule file sits, so this is not the cause.

options.text: Path-scoped rules load only when Claude Code works in plan mode, and the CI job runs Claude Code in direct execution through the -p flag.
options.reason: Path-scoped rules load when Claude Code edits files that match their glob patterns; the mode of execution does not control their loading.

options.text: A YAML frontmatter paths field can name only one directory per rule, so the team needs a separate rule file for each directory with schema files.
options.reason: Glob patterns such as **/*.graphql match files by type across all directories, so a single rule file can cover schema files anywhere in the codebase.
